title: Add presubmit fine-grain throttler and lockfile signer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a presubmit throttler to avoid CI queue storms and a small lockfile signing utility to attest automated dependency updates; improves presubmit resiliency and dependency provenance.
description:
Context: Recent spikes in presubmit traffic and multiple transient dependency rollups caused CI queues to back up and flaky longtests to pile up; automated lockfile updates created occasional confusion about authoritative dependency state. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) a fine-grain presubmit throttler that can rate-limit and weight presubmit job admission per repo/path/label and provides a soft-priority lane for high-value commits; 2) a lockfile signer utility that signs lockfile updates produced by our dep-roller so presubmit flows can quickly determine if a lockfile was ratified by the automated tool. Design summary: throttler is implemented as a lightweight admission proxy in the presubmit runner (presubmit/proxy/throttler.go + config schema presubmit/config/throttle.yaml). It supports token-bucket per-key admission, a small in-memory LRU for burst accounting, and rules that can be scoped by path globs and LABELS (e.g., skip throttle for docs/*). The lockfile signer is a small CLI and library (tools/lock-signer) that integrates with the dep-roller pipeline: it signs lockfile blobs with a short-lived key stored in KMS and emits a signed-metadata.json adjacent to the lockfile; the presubmit agent verifies signature before treating the lockfile as authoritative. Testing and rollout: unit tests added for admission logic and signature verification; end-to-end smoke harness added to perf-canary that exercises throttling under burst load (simulated 600 concurrent presubmits). Rollout plan: feature flag controlled (presubmit.throttle.v1) defaulted to off; flip for a single team then 25% repo sampling over two weeks. Security review: lockfile signer uses existing KMS access patterns; reviewer checklist included below. Implementation checklist: - [x] Implement throttler admission proxy and config parsing - [x] Add unit tests for token-bucket/hotkey handling - [x] Add lockfile signer CLI and verification helper - [x] Add integration smoke to perf-canary - [x] Add feature flag and runtime metrics (throttle.admitted, throttle-rejected, signer.verified) - [x] Update docs/ci-presubmit.md to describe config - [x] Add migration notes for dep-roller to produce signed-metadata.json

Commits summary: commit 1: presubmit: add throttler admission proxy and config schema; commit 2: presubmit: add unit tests and metrics; commit 3: tools: add lockfile signer CLI and verification helper; commit 4: perf-canary: add smoke harness; commit 5: docs: presubmit/lockfile signing docs and rollout notes; commit 6: address reviewer feedback (auth check, config defaults).

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice isolation of admission logic — can we expose a per-repo override via repo-config? Concern: hotspot keys might starve smaller repos.
Maya Chen (author): Added repo-scoped overrides and an LRU-based hotkey backoff; default config continues to protect small repos (see presubmit/config/throttle.yaml).
Priya Nair: Lockfile signer looks good. Two asks: (1) ensure signer keys are auditable and rotated; (2) add a fallback if KMS is unreachable so presubmit doesn't fail hard.

Maya Chen (author): Implemented KMS availability probe with graceful degrade mode (verifier returns 'unverified' but does not block presubmit when feature flag disabled). Added rotation note to docs and linked to security runbook. See commit a8b7c5e.

notes_for_reviewers: Key review points: 1) confirm throttle default config is conservative for small teams; 2) validate KMS usage and signer key lifecycle; 3) review metrics to avoid cardinality explosion. This PR intentionally keeps admission state in-process to minimize latency; if load proves high we will move to a small redis-backed token-bucket - that follow-up will be a separate RFC.
testing_steps: 1) enable presubmit.throttle.v1 for a staging repo; 2) run perf-canary smoke harness (make perf-canary-run) which simulates burst traffic; 3) run tools/lock-signer sign --file=go.sum and verify with tools/lock-signer verify --meta=signed-metadata.json; 4) observe metric throttle.admitted vs throttle.rejected in staging Grafana dashboard.
estimated_impact: Reduces peak presubmit queue lengths by estimated 35-60% in staging based on perf-canary runs; improves confidence in automated lockfile updates by providing cryptographic provenance.
post_deploy_monitoring: Watch metrics throttle.rejected, throttle.admitted, signer.verified and presubmit-queue-latency. Add alert if rejected ratio > 20% and queue latency increases > 2x baseline.
